newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Venezuelan congress reopens with busy schedule.
newsitem.headline: Venezuelan congress reopens with busy schedule.

text.p: Venezuela's congress reopened Tuesday for its second series of ordinary sessions with a long list of pending legislation and amid an atmosphere of fragile government support.

Legislation likely to top the agenda includes: the government's proposed 1997 budget; the Debt Rescue Fund -- from which oil payment windfalls would be used to pay-down foreign debt; and proposals to meet the government's $4 billion debt with the Central Bank. The sessions will last until November 30.

None of the five largest parties in Venezuela's bicameral system hold a majority. Governing coalition Convergence currently enjoys the tacit support of social democrat Democratic Action (AD), Venezuela's largest party, and the left wing Movement to Socialism party (MAS).
In opposition Venezuela's second largest party, christian democrat Copei, is paired with union-based Radical Cause.
